key_insight: A physics-informed graph neural network can decode the surface code by learning syndrome-adaptive edge weights while a discrete Poisson solver produces a single topological scalar that captures the logical-error signal.
engineering_relevance: This offers an exact, parameter-free readout that is simple to implement and can match stronger full-field decoders, making it attractive for scalable quantum error-correction pipelines.
method: Encode the syndrome graph with a GNN that learns edge weights from the observed syndrome.
Solve a discrete Poisson equation to obtain node potentials and edge currents under a hard physics prior.
Read out the logical signal as the difference in current drained by sinks placed on the two code boundaries linked by the logical operator.
evidence_signal: On the rotated surface code under circuit-level depolarising noise, the proposed topological scalar matches the best full-field readout, with stronger gains suggested at larger code distances.
watch_item: Performance depends on the learned metric and boundary placement, so robust training and solver integration are important for stable deployment.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for Surface Code Decoding via Discrete Exterior Calculus
